To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
We have developed a new method of fabricating PEDOT films that are free standing, highly conductive, and electrically tuneable.

free standing PEDOT membranes were successfully fabricated using vapour phase deposition, these membranes were conductive and permeable to drug molecules, and the permeability of the drug molecules was electrically tuneable.

we have fabricated freestanding PEDOP films by vapour phase oxidation of EDOT and that these films are highly conductive (1840±50 S/cm) and can be electrically modulated to control the permeability of small drug molecules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of electrically tuneable membranes for drug delivery and molecular separation.
the development of novel materials for use in the controlled release of drugs.
the development of electrically tuneable membranes for the control of molecular transport and the development of electric field driven drug delivery systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PEDOT films were electrically modifiable and could be used as electrically tune-able drug permeation membranes.
the PEDOT films are highly conductive and flexible, they can be used to control drug permeation, and the vapour phase polymerization is a useful method to produce PEDOT films.
the PEDOT membranes have the ability to electrically tune the permeability of small molecules, and are a promising material for drug delivery and separation applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that PEDOT films prepared using vapour phase oxidation and doping can be used as electrically tune able membranes to control drug permeability.
we have shown for the first time that vapour phase polymerised PEDOT films can be used as electrically tune-able barriers to drug diffusion.
the vapour phase polymerised PEDOT films were electrically tuneable membranes that can be used to control the permeability of small molecules, but not large molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PEDOT films are highly permeable to small molecules, however, the size of the molecule dictates the extent of permeability.
the PEDOT films can be used as a rate controlling barrier for small molecules and the permeation can be controlled electrically.
PEDOT is an excellent candidate material to be used as an electrically tunable rate controlling membrane.
